documents.title: Prompt injection defense notes
documents.text: Prompt injection is untrusted content that attempts to override system instructions or make a model reveal secrets or misuse tools. Treat retrieved documents and user-provided text as data, not as higher-priority instructions.

documents.title: AI tool action authorization policy
documents.text: Sensitive tool actions must be checked by an independent authorization layer outside the language model. Use an explicit allowlist, validate arguments, grant least privilege, and require human approval for high-impact actions.

documents.title: Privacy-conscious audit logging
documents.text: Privacy-conscious AI audit logs record timestamps, request identifiers, event types, policy decisions, and rule identifiers. Avoid storing raw prompts, responses, credentials, and unnecessary personal data by default. Hashes are not anonymization.

documents.title: Evidence retrieval provenance
documents.text: Retrieval provenance records source identity, title, publisher, supplied publication and retrieval dates, source URI, document hash, chunk hash, and character offsets so retrieved passages can be traced to ingested source versions.

documents.title: Natural language inference evaluation notes
documents.text: Natural language inference models classify a premise and hypothesis as entailment, contradiction, or neutral. Their scores can be wrong and are not calibrated probabilities unless validated. Evidence relevance is not proof that a factual claim is supported.

documents.title: API credential handling policy
documents.text: API keys and gateway tokens should be stored in server-side environment variables or a managed secrets store. Never commit credentials to a source repository or expose provider keys in browser or mobile clients.
